Package com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.keycloak

Class SystemdProviderFactory

java.lang.Object
com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.keycloak.SystemdProviderFactory
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.keycloak.provider.ProviderFactory<SystemdProvider>
public class SystemdProviderFactory extends Object implements org.keycloak.provider.ProviderFactory<SystemdProvider>
Integrates Keycloak with systemd, following the life cycle of Keycloak:
  1. when Keycloak initializes its providers, at the start of its bootstrap, the integration starts, and the status shows Startup: bootstrapping;
  2. while Keycloak bootstraps, the steps of the bootstrap that can be followed are shown in the status, and extend the startup timeout: each changeset of the database migration, which LiquibaseProgressProviderFactory follows, each realm that is imported, and anything else that Keycloak publishes an event for;
  3. once Keycloak has completed its bootstrap, which includes migrating the database and importing realms, and its HTTP server listens, systemd is told that Keycloak is ready. Either may happen last: Keycloak bootstraps once its HTTP server listens when the health endpoints are enabled, answering 503 until then, and before it starts its HTTP server otherwise. When the health endpoints are enabled, Keycloak is also only ready once its readiness health checks, those of its /health/ready endpoint, are all up;
  4. as soon as Keycloak is told to stop, systemd is told that it is stopping, and the status shows Shutdown: stopping;
  5. once Keycloak closes its providers, the integration stops.

The watchdog heartbeats are sent when the service unit sets WatchdogSec, taking into account the health conditions that are opted into, none by default, and the status shows the status of Keycloak and of the JVM.

Author:
Joao Silva
